question: Chadwick's 1842 report said Liverpool labourers died at an average age of 15. What does that figure mostly reflect?
options: Most labourers dying in their teens
Huge numbers of deaths in infancy
Labourers leaving town before old age
answer: Huge numbers of deaths in infancy. An average age at death pools every death, and in poor districts a large share of children died before five, dragging the mean down. A fast-growing town full of young migrants also produces young deaths. Those who survived childhood lived far beyond 15. Many of those coffins were small.
move: Before trusting an average, ask what the extremes are doing to it.
trap: Reading an average age at death as a typical lifespan.
source: Chadwick, Sanitary Condition of the Labouring Population, 1842
reference: Chadwick, Report on the Sanitary Condition of the Labouring Population of Great Britain, 1842; ed. Flinn, Edinburgh University Press, 1965
